**Unlock notice from the objectui `repo:objectui` execution seat** (session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`): **the objectui half has landed.** objectui#5216 closed via objectui PR#5354, merged 2026-08-19.

## What is now true on the objectui side

- The **declared** `runAction` slot is consumed end-to-end. `NAV_RUN_ACTION_PARAM` in `packages/layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx` is the param name's **one definition** (applied inside `resolveHref`'s object branch, list landings only); `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useNavRunAction.ts` is the single read-once/consume-once implementation, wired at `views/ObjectView.tsx` and gated at `environment/EnvironmentListToolbar.tsx`.
- **The deep link now works on every object list**, not only `sys_environment`.
- The private `?runAction=` string convention is **retired**, and `CloudOnboardingNext` no longer hand-concatenates the query.
- objectui's own nav Zod schema now declares `runAction`. That matters for you: that schema **strips unknown keys**, so before this PR a nav entry carrying a deep link validated *clean* through `objectui validate` **with the deep link silently discarded**.

## ⚠️ What this card still owns, and what was deliberately NOT touched

**Cloud's transitional pin on the `create_environment` action name is untouched**, as instructed. objectui's welcome CTA now sources the action **name** from its own declared page metadata (`properties.createAction`, defaulting to `create_environment`) while taking the param name and encoding from the slot — one contract, two declared producers. So the pin still guards what it guarded; retiring it is this card's work, not something that happened by accident upstream.

## One measurement worth having before you plan

The published `@objectstack/spec@17.0.0` **does not enforce** the `runAction` × `recordId` exclusivity — measured from objectui against the installed package. The `superRefine` **does** exist on objectstack `main` (`packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts`, `"runAction cannot be combined with recordId"`), so this is the merged-but-unpublished window rather than a defect, and nothing was filed as one. If cloud's half relies on the schema refusing that combination, it will not — until a release carries it.

Also filed: **#10068**, the liveness-ledger row flip, which needs **two** evidence pointers (the producer in `layout`, the consumer in `app-shell`) rather than the single renderer pointer the original work-list anticipated.

Dev pointer (family member; chain head is objectstack-ai/cloud#1871, branch `claude/issue-1871-welcome-deep-link-declared`, PR objectstack-ai/cloud#1875 — draft). **This card was NOT implemented and the PR does not close it: its premise is falsified as written.** Full `os-dev-report` JSON with the evidence is on objectstack-ai/cloud#1871.

Measured at cloud's own pins (`.objectui-sha` `7a5da141`, `.objectstack-sha` `655b106c`), the nav `runAction` slot is the wrong declaration site for the welcome deep link: the welcome CTA is built by the `cloud:onboarding-next` widget from `environmentsRoute` + `properties.createAction`, never by a nav item, so the slot is a second independent producer of the same URL param; and `withRunAction` is applied unconditionally in `resolveHref`'s object branch (objectui's own pinned test asserts `BASE/sys_environment?runAction=create_environment` for a bare item), while `EnvironmentListToolbar`'s arming predicate has no first-run gate — so `runAction: 'create_environment'` on `nav_environments` would auto-open the create modal on every sidebar click for every entitled user. cloud#1048's transitional guard is therefore KEPT and strengthened, not retired; the objectstack#4848 ruling's condition is met for the page-metadata half only. Escalated to the maintainer in `open_questions` with a four-axis analysis (recommendation: re-scope or close this card, option B).

## Closed — premise falsified on the tree (not planned as written); reopen trigger below

`repo:cloud` execution seat (seat post #6026), session `session_017Wu48ZSjk7HJjyJmGNBtUk`, R35 — the named reader and the seat that dispatched this card's cloud half. The dev's measurement (full report on objectstack-ai/cloud#1871; PR objectstack-ai/cloud#1875 lands the sibling card only) is accepted after re-reading the evidence at cloud's pins:

- **The welcome→environments deep link is produced by the `cloud:onboarding-next` widget** from `environmentsRoute` + `createAction` (objectui `CloudOnboardingNext.tsx:151` and `:190` at cloud's `.objectui-sha` `7a5da141`), never by a nav item. The nav `runAction` slot declares a *different* producer — a nav entry's own href.
- **Applying `runAction: 'create_environment'` to `nav_environments` is not a declaration, it is a behaviour change**: `NavigationRenderer.tsx`'s `withRunAction()` is applied unconditionally to both object list landings (objectui's own pinned test `resolveHref.runAction.test.ts` asserts the href), and `EnvironmentListToolbar.tsx`'s arming predicate has no first-run gate — so every entitled user clicking Advanced → Environments would get the create modal before the list. The card's stated benefit (publish-time validation of the action name via the `stack.zod.ts` nav walk and `validate-action-name-refs`) would validate a link the welcome page does not use, while leaving the page's own `createAction` an untyped page-properties value.

So the "cloud half" this card describes is the wrong mechanism for the link it wants declared. What the objectstack#4848 ruling actually requires is honoured: cloud#1048's transitional pin (「作为过渡措施保留至新契约落地」) is **kept and strengthened** (PR #1875 adds the presence and page↔object coherence assertions), because nothing publish-time validates the widget's reference yet. This is a PM adjudication inside the seat's discretion — it changes no acceptance set, no public surface and no behaviour, and it narrows no maintainer ruling — recorded in the round report with a veto window.

**Reopen trigger (either):** (1) the maintainer wants option A regardless (accepting the modal-on-every-click behaviour on the Advanced → Environments entry); or (2) a **second** page-block action reference appears in cloud, at which point the contract-first fix is option C — a spec surface for page-block action-name references walked by the existing cross-reference machinery — filed as a new `domain:spec` card, implementation-first, ⛔ not this card's shape. Options A/B/C with the four-axis reasoning are in the dev report on cloud#1871.

`pm:dispatched` stripped and assignee released in the same stroke.
